acceptanceCriteria: The amend API supports schema-aware add, set, clear, remove, replace, and reorder operations for all human-owned plan fields, with per-operation reason, expected prior digest, full Contract validation, and all-or-nothing application.

Identity, observed repository/environment facts, lifecycle state, and immutable evidence cannot be rewritten by generic amend; authority-sensitive or gate-weakening changes trigger the corresponding reauthorization and review gates.

Each amendment leaves append-only, verifiable old/new values and digests, rationale, sequence, environment/repository snapshot binding, and evidence-impact record; interruption and retry cannot lose or duplicate a committed change.

Runtime records environment drift explicitly from observed execution facts and fans out relevant invalidations to active Work Items through shared repository state; admission refreshes immediately before affected actions, stale generations cannot execute, and unaffected actions remain admissible.

CLI and MCP expose equivalent write and read surfaces; single-WI serial lifecycle continues to work; actual concurrent processes in multiple linked worktrees prove drift handling, selective blocking, recovery, and stale-receipt rejection.
English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese command and Contract guidance describe amendment and environment-change semantics without claiming unsupported behavior.
goal: Agents can revise any human-owned plan decision with an explicit reason and traceable history. Runtime-observed environment changes refresh shared execution context, invalidate only affected action admissions, and allow unrelated work to continue; authorization and verification are re-evaluated, never bypassed.
intent: Enable reality-driven and auditable evolution of active Work Item plans, including coordinated response to environment drift across parallel Work Items.
outOfScope: changes to WI-1040 or WI-1041 records
manual edits to Runtime-generated records or bypassing schema and admission

scenarioCoverage.expected: All supported operations update only registered human-owned fields; identity and Runtime facts remain immutable, while sensitive changes re-run policy and review.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Protocol and repository tests for all operations, invalid paths, digest conflicts, policy effects, and full Contract validation.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Concurrent and interrupted amendment attempts are idempotent or conflict explicitly; no partial, lost, duplicated, or rewritten audit history is visible.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Crash-injection and two-process tests across every persistence boundary, including same changeId replay.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A changed runtime-observed environment persists across processes; affected actions are denied before side effects, and unrelated outcomes remain admissible.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Real CLI processes in multiple linked worktrees over one common directory, with changed environment and unchanged submitted Contract JSON.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Runtime 0.2.113 cannot silently ignore amendment or drift constraints; old generations cannot act and recovery is append-only across generation advance.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Compatibility tests against the exact 0.2.113 Runtime identity plus stale-generation and recovery regressions.

scenarioCoverage.expected: CLI and MCP expose equivalent write/read semantics, and agent interface/guidance accurately advertise them.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: CLI/MCP contract tests and manifest/documentation acceptance tests.

scenarioCoverage.expected: The ordinary single-Work-Item serial path remains available and English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese guidance agrees.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Serial lifecycle acceptance plus canonical docs parity and documentation acceptance.
